label: Formulated the pedagogy of the oppressed and dialogical problem-posing education
description: Freire established critical pedagogy by rejecting the authoritarian banking model of education and creating a method where learners decode social reality into transformative praxis.
historicalContext: Developed during mass adult literacy campaigns in Northeastern Brazil in the early 1960s and codified during his exile in Chile (1968).
dialecticalTension: Overcomes the contradiction between teacher (as absolute possessor of knowledge) and student (as passive depository) through mutual dialogical inquiry.

citations.author: Paulo Freire
citations.quote: Education must begin with the solution of the teacher-student contradiction, by reconciling the poles of the contradiction so that both are simultaneously teachers and students.

citations.author: Henry A. Giroux
citations.work: Teachers as Intellectuals: Toward a Critical Pedagogy of Learning

label: Applied historical-materialist alienation to pedagogical praxis
description: Freire adapted Marx's concepts of alienation, historical consciousness, and praxis—insisting that human reflection without action is mere verbalism, and action without reflection is blind activism.
historicalContext: Formulated in dialogue with 20th-century Latin American Marxist liberation movements and Third World solidarity struggles.
dialecticalTension: Transforms Marxist structural analysis into an educational and dialogical method centered on humanization rather than vanguardist coercion.

citations.author: Paulo Freire
citations.quote: Functionally, oppression is domesticating. To no longer be prey to its force, one must emerge from it and turn upon it. This can be done only by means of the praxis: reflection and action upon the world in order to transform it.

citations.author: Peter McLaren
citations.work: Che Guevara, Paulo Freire, and the Pedagogy of Revolution

label: Integrated Fanonian psychology of colonial internalization
description: Freire drew directly on Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth to explain how the oppressed internalize the image of the oppressor, producing an existential duality that fears authentic freedom.
historicalContext: Freire read Fanon intensely while writing Pedagogy of the Oppressed in Santiago, Chile in 1967–1968.
dialecticalTension: Deepens Fanon's critique of the internalized colonizer by providing an educational praxis for therapeutic and political de-alienation.

citations.author: Paulo Freire
citations.quote: The oppressed suffer from the duality which has established itself in their innermost being... They have adopted the guidelines of the oppressor.

citations.author: Lewis R. Gordon
citations.work: What Fanon Said: A Philosophical Introduction to His Life and Thought

label: Supplied the pedagogical and dialogical foundation for the Philosophy of Liberation
description: Dussel incorporated Freire's dialogical problem-posing praxis as the pedagogical moment of liberation philosophy, connecting theoretical ethics with popular consciousness.
historicalContext: Both thinkers collaborated in Latin American liberation philosophy circles and ecumenical reflection groups throughout the 1970s.
dialecticalTension: Extends Freire's educational pedagogy into a comprehensive geopolitical architecture of Latin American transmodern ethics.

citations.author: Enrique Dussel
citations.quote: Freire has clearly demonstrated how the teacher-student relation can reproduce domination or unleash the liberating Word.

citations.author: Walter D. Mignolo
citations.work: The Darker Side of Western Modernity: Global Futures, Decolonial Options
